note_sections.t: Re-evaluation for prostate cancer management decision following stable Gleason 3+3 biopsy with high-risk features and rising PSA.

The patient is a 65-year-old retired shopkeeper who presents for re-evaluation of his prostate cancer diagnosis. He reports no urinary symptoms, with an IPSS score of 5/35 indicating mild LUTS. He is married and lives in a ground-floor apartment with his partner, who is supportive of his care. He is an avid cyclist, commuting five times a week, and abstains from alcohol. He has no significant comorbidities and takes no regular medications. His PSA has risen from 2.5 ng/mL in May 2023 to 4.53 ng/mL in February 2025, with a dip to 1.5 ng/mL in December 2023. He expresses significant anxiety about invasive procedures and has requested a thorough discussion of all options. His adult son is the primary next-of-kin contact and is involved in care discussions.

On DRE, the prostate is smooth and symmetric with no palpable nodules or asymmetry, consistent with clinical stage cT1c. General examination reveals a well-nourished male with stable vital signs and no lymphadenopathy. Abdominal examination is unremarkable with no organomegaly or masses.
